usageNotes: Use this to apply pending network configuration changes on a node without rebooting — it reloads the interfaces file and restarts the networking stack. The node must be online and reachable, and the caller requires Sys.Modify on /nodes/{node}. Set regenerate-frr to true only if you use SDN/FRR-based routing and need the FRR daemon config rebuilt from the current SDN config.

examples.summary: Reload network config on pve1 and regenerate FRR routing config

tips: This reloads the live networking stack — brief packet loss on active interfaces is expected during the reload.
Use POST /nodes/{node}/network to stage interface changes first; PUT applies all pending changes at once.
If the node has SDN zones configured, pass regenerate-frr: true to ensure FRR picks up any route/peer changes.
The return value is a plain string (e.g. an empty string or status message), not a task UPID — the reload is synchronous from the API's perspective.
